newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Silicon to participate in Malaysia's MSC.
newsitem.headline: Silicon to participate in Malaysia's MSC.

text.p: Silicon Graphics Inc's Malaysian unit said on Tuesday that it intended to participate in Malaysia's Multimedia Super Corridor (MSC), the national Bernama news agency reported.

"We are planning to register with the MSC secretariat but first we want to have a direct presence here and to understand what we can contribute to the MSC," Bernama quoted Silicon Graphics Sdn Bhd branch manager Abdul Wahab Yusoff as saying.
He was speaking to reporters after the official opening of the company's Kuala Lumpur office on Tuesday.
Company officials were not immediately available for comment.
Malaysia has invited companies to start applying for MSC status to set up businesses in the corridor starting from next month.

Robert Bishop, chairman of Silicon Graphics' Silicon Graphics World Trade, last month joined a group of other high-technology executives to discuss the massive MSC project with Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad.
Silicon Graphics is based in Mountain View, California. Its products include computer workstations and supercomputers.
Bishop is on the MSC's International Advisory Panel.
The corridor, a nine-by-30 mile (15-by-50 km) zone extending south from Kuala Lumpur, is being designated as a high-tech centre.
By the year 2000, the corridor should provide leading applications like telemedicine, smart schools and other services.
On Monday, Mahathir said about 400 international and local companies have indicated interest in the project so far.
Silicon Graphic's activities in Malaysia include supplying supercomputers to local universities.
